ellie-newhire: Hey all — quick question about 401k for my first pay. I started mid-cycle (3/18) and my first paycheck covered only 3 days. I already set 6% in onboarding. Is the company match prorated on that first partial paycheck or does match wait until the full month? Also I'm under 50 but wanted to know if catch-up rules ever get pro-rated. thanks!

sarah-peopleops: welcome @ellie-newhire! short answer: match is typically applied to each payroll based on the deferral actually taken on that paycheck. so if you contributed 6% of the partial pay, the employer match for that check is 6% of the wages in that pay (subject to plan rules). :+1:

ellie-newhire: awesome — so even if the dollar amount is small because it's only 3 days, the match still shows up proportional to that check?

mike-payroll: correct. payroll vendor PayDesk calculates match per pay period. example: if gross for partial check = $1,200 and your 6% deferral = $72, and plan matches 100% up to 4%, they'd match 4% of $1,200 = $48 (if code uses limit at match percentage). some plans match on actual deferral amount (so we'd match $72 up to cap) — depends on what the plan document says. i'll double-check our plan spec.

julia-finance: to add — most of our contributions are processed per-paycheck and then sent in a batch to the recordkeeper at month-end. that means the match will appear on the payroll side immediately and then post to the plan account after remittance. it won't get held back until you hit a full month.

ellie-newhire: thanks — and what about catch-up contributions (50+). if someone turns 50 mid-year, do they get a pro-rated higher limit or is it calendar year based?

sarah-peopleops: catch-up contributions are an annual limit that the IRS governs. there is no pro‑rata increase; the catch-up dollar amount is based on the plan year/calendar year (you can contribute up to the catch-up limit for the year once eligible). so turning 50 midyear doesn't reduce your ability to contribute the full catch-up amount, but practical limits depend on payroll processing and whether you elect higher deferrals for the remainder of the year.

mike-payroll: operational note: if someone becomes eligible midyear and wants to contribute catch-up dollars, we can increase their per-paycheck deferral to hit the limit, but they must update elections in PayPortal before the payroll cutoff. if they miss the cutoff, the change applies the next pay period.

ellie-newhire: perfect. last thing — our recordkeeper for the plan (AscendRetire) has a weird rule about minimum per-contribution dollar amounts. could that block a tiny match on a partial pay?

julia-finance: good catch. AscendRetire has a $1 minimum per contribution type in some cases. if a match amount would be less than $1, we reconcile it at month-end and either roll it into the next contribution or combine with other micro-matches. i'll confirm the exact behavior for our employer match.

mike-payroll: i'll run the partial-check example through a dry run today and DM the results. if anything gets held, we'll adjust with a catch-up micro payment so the employee isn't disadvantaged.

sarah-peopleops: action items: (1) @mike-payroll confirm whether PayDesk sends micro amounts to AscendRetire or if they aggregate, (2) @julia-finance confirm AscendRetire $1 minimum behavior for employer match, (3) @ellie-newhire if you want, i can walk through changing deferrals to hit target contribution for the year.

onboarding-bot: Welcome message sent to ellie-newhire. New hire checklist: benefits enrollment completed. :tada:

ellie-newhire: thanks everyone — appreciate the clarity. i'll wait for the dry run and may tweak elections. :smile:
